message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p2 with $578 and a dark blue monopoly on Park Place and Boardwalk. I have one house on Boardwalk.

Recalculating cash: $578 after mortgaging Penn RR and Water Works. The prior plan was to mortgage St Charles and Vermont for $195, build two houses on Boardwalk and Park Place for $600, leaving about $98. Kentucky would stay unmortgaged as a backstop.

The prior plan assumed $503 cash and unmortgaged Water Works. The current state shows $578 cash with both Penn RR and Water Works mortgaged. This means the last thought was written before the Water Works mortgage was applied.

The current state is the source of truth. I can only build on Park Place to even the houses with Boardwalk. Each dark blue house costs $200.

Mortgaging St Charles and Vermont for $120 will raise cash to $698. That covers the $600 needed for three houses on the dark blue set, leaving a $98 buffer.

I'm checking whether the engine allows a single build plan with multiple items. The goal is to build one house on Park Place, one on Boardwalk, and one more on Park Place to reach two houses each. Even-building rules may require sequential validation or final-state checks.

I'll mortgage St Charles first for $70, then Vermont for $50 on the next turn. This keeps cash at $698 before building. I'm now checking whether two houses on each dark blue property is the right target.

Two houses on each dark blue property would yield $600 on Boardwalk and $500 on Park Place. The opponents have $664, $867, and $951 cash respectively, so neither bankruptcy nor immediate mortgage is guaranteed. This validates the target.

Mortgaging all three unmortgaged properties would raise cash to $808, allowing four houses on the dark blue set. That would bankrupt every opponent with a single rent. The safer path is two houses each, leaving about $98 after building. I'm now checking whether that buffer survives the upcoming income tax of $200.

The luxury tax is $100. Other players have no monopolies with houses, so rent is low. I already landed on Reading Railroad and auctioned it, so I won't pay rent this turn. I may roll from Reading next turn. Jail is possible.

I'm at Reading Railroad (space 5) and must travel almost a full lap to reach GO. I'll pass several properties on the way. The next roll could land me on Connecticut, Oriental, or Electric depending on the dice.

The $98 buffer is too small for luxury tax. A Chairman of the Board card would cost $150, and house repairs could cost $40 or more. The previous strategy already avoided a three-and-two build because it leaves only about $8.

I will keep Kentucky unmortgaged as a $110 backstop and red block. I am blocking the red, pink, and light blue monopolies by holding key properties that complete them.

I rejected building one house now because the rent would be too weak. I will mortgage St Charles for $70 and wait for the next turn to mortgage Vermont before building.
